why: In every figure the circle and the square sit on opposite sides: one is in the left half and the other is in the right half. Figures 1, 2, 3 and 5 follow this (circle left and square right, or circle right and square left). In figure 4 the circle and the square are both on the right side, one above the other. So figure 4 breaks the rule. Figure 3 looks different because the circle is low, but it still has the circle on the left and the square on the right.
trick: Ignore up and down moves first and check left or right sides of each shape. The figure where both shapes are on the same side is the odd one.
note: Rule inferred: shapes on opposite sides. Alternative reading (circle at top) would make 3 odd, but 4 fits the side rule best.
